phases.name: Establish request and location paths
phases.description: Separate the frozen brief from design assumptions, then connect rider and driver clients to the matching boundary.

phases.name: Find and rank eligible drivers
phases.description: Use fresh geospatial state and durable trip data to shortlist candidates by service type, distance, wait, ratings, and surge.

phases.name: Offer, accept, and retry safely
phases.description: Buffer matching work, prevent double assignment, notify drivers, and return live status while rejected or expired offers re-enter matching.

phases.name: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
phases.description: Make concurrency and scale behavior explicit, measure the seconds-level objective, and identify policies the brief leaves open.

steps.title: Read the brief before choosing targets
steps.content: Frozen problem: Find a Rider for Uber or Uber Eats. Brief: Design a matching algorithm to efficiently connect riders/customers with drivers in real-time. Requirements: Match riders with nearby drivers; Optimize for wait time and distance; Handle simultaneous requests; Driver acceptance and timeout; Prioritize based on ratings and surge; Support different service types (pool, premium); Handle millions of matches per day; Real-time location tracking. Constraints: Match within seconds; Balance driver utilization; Handle driver rejections; Minimize rider wait time; Fair matching algorithm. The brief gives no exact QPS, location-update cadence, offer deadline, retention period, fairness formula, or numeric latency percentile. All technology and policy choices below are assumptions for review, not facts from the brief.

steps.title: Add the rider client
steps.content: Represent the rider app that submits a pickup, destination, and requested service class, then receives an offer or assignment state. Validate the actual request fields and consent rules with the product API; the brief does not specify them.

component.label: Rider App
component.description: Requests a ride and receives matching status

properties.purpose: Submit a pickup and service-class request; display pending, matched, and failed states from the server.

component.highlightReason: The existing Mobile App catalog component represents the rider client; no new component type is needed.

steps.title: Add the driver client
steps.content: Represent the driver app as the source of availability, location updates, offer responses, and live assignment status. Location freshness and background-update behavior are open product and platform decisions.

component.label: Driver App
component.description: Publishes driver state and accepts or rejects offers

properties.purpose: Send authenticated location and availability updates, receive eligible offers, and return an idempotent accept or reject response.

component.highlightReason: The same supported Mobile App component models a second client role without inventing a catalog node.

steps.title: Add the authenticated matching API
steps.content: Use the API boundary to authenticate rider and driver requests, validate coordinates and service class, apply abuse controls, and attach idempotency keys to retried ride requests and offer responses.

component.label: Matching API Gateway
component.description: Validates and routes rider and driver traffic

properties.purpose: Authenticate clients, validate request shape and service class, enforce rate limits, and route location, ride-request, and offer-response APIs.

component.highlightReason: API Gateway is a supported catalog component with authentication, validation, and throttling properties.

steps.title: Send rider requests through the API
steps.content: The rider submits a request through the authenticated API. Return a request identifier immediately, but do not report a match until an eligible driver has accepted and the assignment is committed.

connection.label: Ride request + service class
connection.description: Authenticated, idempotent request with pickup and requested service type

steps.title: Send driver location and offer responses
steps.content: Use one client-to-API path for timestamped location/availability updates and explicit accept or reject responses. Reject stale or out-of-order location updates according to a freshness policy that must be measured and approved.

connection.label: Location + availability + offer response
connection.description: Driver actions are authenticated, timestamped, and safe to retry

steps.title: Add the matching coordinator
steps.content: The coordinator owns request lifecycle and orchestration: validate eligible service class, enqueue matching work, issue offers, and report state. Keep candidate scoring and durable assignment semantics explicit rather than hiding them in a generic API handler.

component.label: Matching Coordinator
component.description: Coordinates requests, offers, and assignment state

properties.purpose: Coordinate request state, candidate ranking, bounded offer rounds, idempotency, and live updates; keep matching policy versioned and testable.

component.highlightReason: Backend Server is the existing catalog fit for application orchestration.

steps.title: Route requests and driver events to matching
steps.content: The coordinator receives both rider requests and driver state changes behind the same authenticated boundary. Partition work by geographic area and service class only as a design assumption; measure skew before fixing partition counts.

connection.label: Validated requests + driver events
connection.description: API forwards idempotency keys, timestamps, and service-class constraints

steps.title: Add a live geospatial driver index
steps.content: Use the supported Cache component as a low-latency geospatial index of currently available drivers, keyed or partitioned by location cell and service eligibility. Treat it as a candidate index, not the durable source of truth for an assignment.

component.label: Live Driver Geo Index
component.description: Finds nearby, recently updated eligible drivers

properties.purpose: Maintain fresh available-driver location and service eligibility in geospatial cells; expire stale entries and return candidates for authoritative validation.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Cache component supports the fast-changing candidate index; its purpose explains the geospatial role without a custom node.

steps.title: Refresh and query nearby driver candidates
steps.content: Location updates refresh the candidate index; matching searches nearby cells and filters by service class and current availability. Apply a freshness cutoff so stale positions cannot be treated as reliable proximity.

connection.label: Location refresh + nearby candidates
connection.description: Fast spatial lookup is advisory; confirm driver state before committing an assignment

steps.title: Choose a reviewable ranking policy
steps.content: Assumption to validate: score only eligible candidates, using estimated pickup time and distance alongside driver utilization, rating, and the applicable surge context. The weights, tie-break rules, and treatment of pooled rides are policy decisions, not supplied by the brief. Keep the score explainable and log its policy version.

decision.question: How should nearby eligible drivers be ranked?
decision.chosen: Use a versioned score that balances pickup ETA and distance with utilization, rating, and applicable surge policy, then apply a deterministic tie-break within a fairness-aware cohort.
decision.chosenReason: This combines the stated optimization and prioritization signals while making utilization and fairness measurable; it avoids claiming that a single nearest-driver rule satisfies all goals.

alternatives.option: Always offer to the closest driver
alternatives.tradeoff: Can repeatedly favor the same drivers and ignore utilization, ratings, surge policy, or service eligibility.

alternatives.option: Run a global optimum over every driver for each request
alternatives.tradeoff: May add coordination latency and contention; benchmark it against bounded regional matching before adopting it.

steps.title: Add durable trip and driver state
steps.content: Keep ride requests, driver availability, offer attempts, and final assignments in durable storage. Enforce valid state transitions and use a conditional write or transaction for exclusive assignment; cache contents alone must never grant a ride.

component.label: Trip & Driver State Database
component.description: Durable request lifecycle and assignment authority

properties.purpose: Persist request and offer state, driver availability, service eligibility, ratings/surge inputs as appropriate, and the authoritative conditional assignment transition.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database catalog component is appropriate for durable state and conditional assignment semantics.

steps.title: Read authoritative state before an offer
steps.content: The coordinator reads durable request and driver state to validate cache candidates, recheck service eligibility, and avoid offering to a driver already assigned or no longer available. Define the transaction and consistency boundary with the chosen database before implementation.

connection.label: Request + eligibility + assignment state
connection.description: Durable state is authoritative for availability and lifecycle transitions

steps.title: Separate service classes during candidate selection
steps.content: Pool and premium requests must not share an undifferentiated candidate set. Apply service eligibility before ranking; pooled-trip compatibility and premium-specific guarantees need explicit product rules. Ratings and surge affect ranking only under an approved, auditable policy.

steps.title: Expand the search without losing the wait objective
steps.content: Assumption to validate: begin with nearby cells and expand the search region when no suitable candidate responds, while honoring a request deadline and service-class constraints. A radius schedule and maximum wait are intentionally left open because the brief provides neither.

decision.question: What should happen when the first local candidate set is empty or declines?
decision.chosen: Expand eligible geospatial cells in bounded rounds, retain the original request age and service class, and stop or offer a clear no-match outcome at an approved deadline.
decision.chosenReason: This provides a controlled path to minimize wait without silently broadening eligibility or waiting indefinitely.

alternatives.option: Search only the first cell once
alternatives.tradeoff: Can fail to match despite nearby eligible drivers just outside the initial boundary.

alternatives.option: Expand until any driver is found with no deadline
alternatives.tradeoff: Can violate service eligibility and leave riders waiting without a bound.

steps.title: Add a durable matching work queue
steps.content: Use a queue to decouple incoming requests from matching execution, absorb bursts, and re-enqueue a request after a rejection or offer expiry. Preserve request age, attempt identity, and service class across retries.

component.label: Matching & Retry Queue
component.description: Buffers requests and bounded retry work

properties.purpose: Durably buffer matching requests and retry events with request identity, age, service class, and attempt number; make rejection and expiry visible to workers.

component.highlightReason: The supported Queue component matches asynchronous dispatch and retry work.

steps.title: Enqueue matching work
steps.content: A validated request becomes durable work before asynchronous matching begins. Expose queue age and oldest-request age so backpressure is visible instead of turning into silent wait-time growth.

connection.label: Idempotent request + retry work
connection.description: Durable work item keeps original age, requested service, and offer-attempt state

steps.title: Add horizontally scalable match workers
steps.content: Workers consume bounded batches, find and rank candidates, create offers, and schedule the next attempt only after a rejection or expiry. Partition by region and service class as an assumption, while monitoring hot cells and keeping request age in the scheduling policy.

component.label: Candidate & Offer Workers
component.description: Ranks candidates and advances matching attempts

properties.purpose: Consume matching work, filter eligible candidates, rank with a versioned policy, create bounded offers, and requeue rejected or expired requests.

component.highlightReason: Processing Worker is a supported catalog component for independently scalable matching work.

steps.title: Dispatch queued work to workers
steps.content: Scale workers against queue age and arrival rate; keep retries bounded and idempotent. A worker crash must leave work available for redelivery without duplicating an accepted assignment.

connection.label: Matching jobs + rejected/expired retries
connection.description: At-least-once delivery is handled with idempotent job and assignment state

steps.title: Give workers candidate and authoritative state access
steps.content: Workers use the geo index to shortlist nearby eligible drivers and durable storage to revalidate each candidate and record the offer attempt. Apply the ranking policy only to the correct service class and retain the decision inputs needed for fairness review.

connection.label: Fresh nearby eligible candidates
connection.description: Candidate lookup is bounded by region, freshness, and requested service type

steps.title: Claim drivers and commit one assignment
steps.content: Before treating an offer as assigned, atomically transition the request and driver state using conditional writes or a transaction. A competing worker or simultaneous request must lose cleanly, then refresh candidates; an accepted offer is not success until this commit wins.

connection.label: Offer lease + exclusive assignment
connection.description: Conditional state transition prevents duplicate driver or request assignment

steps.title: Add the driver offer notification path
steps.content: Deliver an offer with a stable offer identifier, request context permitted for the driver, and an explicit expiry. The offer window is a configurable assumption that must be tuned against the match-within-seconds objective and driver response data.

component.label: Driver Offer Notifications
component.description: Delivers offers and response state to drivers

properties.purpose: Deliver an idempotent, expiring offer to the selected driver and report delivery/response state without making notification delivery the assignment authority.

component.highlightReason: Notification Service is an existing catalog component suitable for push delivery.

steps.title: Send selected-driver offers
steps.content: Only notify a driver after the offer attempt is recorded. Treat duplicate notifications and callbacks as the same offer; on a rejection or expiry, mark that attempt terminal and enqueue the next eligible candidate round.

connection.label: Selected driver offer + expiry
connection.description: Stable offer ID supports idempotent delivery and response reconciliation

steps.title: Deliver the offer to the driver app
steps.content: Push delivery wakes the driver client; the client fetches current offer details and submits accept or reject through the authenticated API. Do not rely on push delivery order or a client-side timer as the source of truth.

connection.label: Offer notification
connection.description: Driver retrieves authoritative offer state and responds through the API

steps.title: Stream matching status to both clients
steps.content: Use a persistent client update channel for pending, offer, accepted, and no-match state. Reconnects must fetch the latest durable state; delivery can be repeated and is not proof that a driver accepted.

connection.label: Ride status updates
connection.description: Rider receives server-owned status and can recover by fetching the request state

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Return offer and assignment status to the driver
steps.content: The coordinator streams the current offer lifecycle to the driver app. Accept/reject still travels through the API and is serialized by the durable state transition, so a late response cannot resurrect an expired offer.

connection.label: Offer lifecycle + assignment state
connection.description: Live view is recoverable from authoritative persisted state

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Make simultaneous requests safe
steps.content: Assumption to validate: every ride request and offer response has an idempotency key; workers may process queue deliveries more than once; and one durable conditional transition arbitrates a driver claimed by competing requests. Define recovery for database timeouts and ambiguous commit outcomes before launch.

decision.question: How do concurrent requests avoid assigning one driver twice?
decision.chosen: Use durable request/offer identifiers and an atomic conditional assignment transition; losers reload state and continue with another candidate rather than assuming success.
decision.chosenReason: Queue delivery and network responses can repeat or race. A single authoritative transition makes the winner explicit and supports safe retries.

alternatives.option: Trust the in-memory worker's candidate list
alternatives.tradeoff: Other workers and regions can concurrently select the same driver.

alternatives.option: Treat client acceptance as the final assignment
alternatives.tradeoff: A late or duplicated response can conflict with an already expired or reassigned offer.

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Scale on queue age and matching latency
steps.content: Millions of matches per day is the stated volume, but the peak rate and geographic skew are unspecified. Load-test arrival bursts and hot cells before choosing partition counts or capacity.

scaleTrigger.metric: Oldest matching-queue age, queue depth by region/service class, and request-to-committed-assignment latency
scaleTrigger.action: Scale candidate workers horizontally and rebalance hot geographic partitions; shed or defer non-critical work before delaying active matching
scaleTrigger.impact: Keeps worker capacity responsive to bursts while exposing whether the seconds-level objective is actually met

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Add matching-path observability
steps.content: Observe request age and outcomes by region and service class, candidate count and pickup distance, location freshness, offer delivery/accept/reject/expiry, worker lag, assignment conflicts, match wait time, utilization, and fairness measures. Avoid retaining precise location longer than an approved policy allows.

component.label: Matching SLO & Fairness Monitoring
component.description: Measures latency, retries, utilization, and assignment quality

properties.purpose: Track queue age, end-to-end match latency, candidate pickup distance, location freshness, candidate and offer outcomes, assignment conflicts, driver utilization, and reviewed fairness indicators.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring is an existing catalog component; its configured metrics and alerts make the stated constraints measurable.

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Observe queue and worker behavior
steps.content: Export processed match volume, queue age, worker lag, retry counts, and regional/service-class partitions so scaling and deadline behavior can be evaluated against real traffic.

connection.label: Queue age + retry lag
connection.description: Queue pressure and retries are visible by region and service class

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Observe match outcomes and fairness
steps.content: Export end-to-end match latency, candidate pickup distance, offer outcomes, assignment conflicts, utilization, and reviewed fairness indicators. Use aggregates and access controls so operational metrics do not become an unintended location-history store.

connection.label: Latency + outcomes + utilization
connection.description: Worker and assignment quality signals support SLO and fairness review

steps.phase: Scale, observe, and review open decisions
steps.title: Review assumptions and open questions
steps.content: Assumptions in this draft: mobile clients use an authenticated API; a cache provides a fresh geospatial candidate index; a database can enforce an atomic assignment transition; a queue and horizontally scalable workers handle bursts and retries; and push/WebSocket updates are advisory views over durable state. Open questions: What are peak and regional request rates? What does “within seconds” mean at p50/p95/p99? How often may drivers update location, and what staleness is acceptable? What is the offer deadline and retry/radius-expansion policy? How are pool compatibility, premium guarantees, ratings, surge, utilization, and fairness weighted and audited? Which routing/ETA source is authoritative? What location data retention and recovery objectives are approved? Validate these with stakeholders and load/failure tests; none is settled by the frozen brief.
